text: Lessons 31 and 34 both hinted at this distinction. Today, the formal names: transformations, and actions.
A transformation takes a DataFrame and returns a brand new one, describing one more step in the plan. Filter, select, with column, group by, join — every one of these runs nothing on its own.
An action is what actually triggers real execution — every transformation that led up to it, all at once. Show, count, collect, write — call any of these, and the whole plan finally runs.

Here's why this matters. Chain four transformations together, and none of them run individually. Only when show finally gets called does Spark run all four, together, in one single optimized pass over the data — genuinely more efficient than running each step on its own.

Returns a DataFrame you can keep chaining? Transformation. Finishes something, gives you a real result? Action. Next lesson: SparkSession — the real entry point behind every line of code you've seen so far. See you there.
